SURVEY_CS_TRANSFORMERS.paper_title: A Survey on Efficient Transformers and Long-Sequence Deep Learning Architectures
SURVEY_CS_TRANSFORMERS.abstract: Transformer architectures have achieved state-of-the-art results across natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. However, the standard dot-product attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length O(N^2), imposing substantial computational and memory bottlenecks for long-context documents. This comprehensive survey systematically reviews efficient transformer modifications, categorizing techniques into IO-aware exact computation, rotational relative positional embeddings, low-rank parameter-efficient adaptation, and external knowledge retrieval augmentation.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction to Self-Attention Bottlenecks
sections.text: The standard multi-head self-attention module computes attention weights as softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d))V. Materializing the full N-by-N attention matrix incurs O(N^2) time and GPU SRAM memory traffic, limiting context length in traditional architectures. Researchers have proposed various approaches to mitigate this, ranging from architectural tiling to external retrieval augmentation.

sections.heading: 2. IO-Aware Hardware Acceleration
sections.text: Rather than approximating attention, IO-aware algorithms reorganize computation to account for GPU memory hierarchy levels between high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and fast static RAM (SRAM). By tiling queries, keys, and values into blocks and computing softmax incrementally via online normalizers, memory reads and writes are reduced by an order of magnitude without any mathematical approximation.

sections.heading: 3. Relative and Rotational Positional Encodings
sections.text: Absolute sinusoidal and learned position embeddings struggle to extrapolate beyond pre-training lengths. Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) resolves this by applying a orthogonal rotation matrix to query and key vectors in 2D sub-spaces, naturally encoding relative distance through inner products while maintaining dot-product efficiency.

sections.heading: 4. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Integration
sections.text: Instead of packing entire external corpora into model context windows, RAG frameworks integrate dense and sparse passage retrievers with pre-trained seq2seq generators, dynamically retrieving non-parametric evidence passages from vector indices to ground factual generation.

P_ATTN_VASWANI.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.

sections.heading: 3.2 Scaled Dot-Product Attention
sections.text: We compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously, packed together into a matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed into matrices K and V. We compute the matrix of outputs as: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V. The two most commonly used attention functions are additive attention and dot-product (multiplicative) attention.

sections.heading: 3.3 Multi-Head Attention
sections.text: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head_1, ..., head_h) W^O where head_i = Attention(Q W_i^Q, K W_i^K, V W_i^V).

P_FLASH_DAO.paper_title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
P_FLASH_DAO.abstract: Transformers are slow and memory-hungry on long sequences, as the time and memory complexity of self-attention is quadratic in sequence length. We propose FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce memory reads/writes between GPU high bandwidth memory (HBM) and GPU on-chip SRAM.

sections.heading: 2. Hardware Characteristics & IO Complexity
sections.text: For modern GPUs like NVIDIA A100 (40-80 GB HBM with 1.5-2.0 TB/s bandwidth, 192 KB on-chip SRAM per SM with 19 TB/s), standard attention execution is memory-bound (memory-access overhead) rather than compute-bound. Standard attention materializes intermediate N x N matrices S and P to HBM, incurring O(N^2) HBM accesses.

sections.heading: 3. Tiling and Online Softmax Normalization
sections.text: FlashAttention computes exact softmax without storing intermediate attention matrices. Given blocks of Q, K, V loaded into on-chip SRAM, we compute local attention and rescale output running accumulators using the online softmax normalization trick: m_new = max(m_prev, x_i) and l_new = exp(m_prev - m_new) l_prev + exp(x_i - m_new).

P_ROPE_SU.paper_title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
P_ROPE_SU.abstract: Positional information is crucial in sequence modeling. We propose Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) to effectively incorporate relative positional interactions into transformer architectures. RoPE encodes relative position by multiplying representations with an orthogonal rotation matrix.

sections.heading: 3. Formulation of Rotary Position Embedding
sections.text: RoPE seeks an inner-product operator g(x_m, x_n, m - n) such that <f(x_m, m), f(x_n, n)> depends only on the relative distance (m - n). By decomposing d-dimensional space into d/2 two-dimensional planes, each 2D vector [x^(2i), x^(2i+1)] is rotated by an angle m*theta_i where theta_i = 10000^(-2(i-1)/d).

sections.heading: 4. Long-Context Decay Property
sections.text: A desirable theoretical property of RoPE is that the inner product between query and key decays naturally as relative distance |m - n| increases, providing an inductive bias for local token affinity while enabling extrapolation.

P_RAG_LEWIS.paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
P_RAG_LEWIS.abstract: Large pre-trained language models store substantial factual knowledge in their parameters, but their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is limited. We explore general-purpose fine-tuning recipes for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combining pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory.

sections.heading: 2. Methods: RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token
sections.text: Our RAG architecture couples a dense passage retriever (DPR) based on bi-encoder BERT with a BART seq2seq generator. Given query x, DPR retrieves top-K candidate documents z. In RAG-Sequence, the same document is used to generate the entire sequence, while RAG-Token allows different documents to condition each generated token.

SURVEY_BIO_STRUCTURAL.paper_title: Machine Learning in Macromolecular Modeling and Protein Structure Prediction: A Review
SURVEY_BIO_STRUCTURAL.abstract: The determination of three-dimensional macromolecular structures from primary amino acid sequences represents a 50-year grand challenge in biophysics. Recent breakthroughs in geometric deep learning, evolutionary covariance representations, and equivariant graph neural networks have fundamentally transformed computational structural biology.

sections.heading: 1. The 50-Year Protein Folding Problem
sections.text: Anfinsen's dogma posited that a protein's native 3D conformation is determined solely by its primary amino acid sequence. Historically, homology modeling and template-based threading failed on novel folds lacking experimental homologs in the PDB.

sections.heading: 2. Multiple Sequence Alignments and Invariant Geometry
sections.text: Co-evolutionary signals in Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) reveal pairwise residue interactions. Modern networks process MSAs with axial attention and refine atomic coordinates using SE(3)-equivariant coordinate frames directly in 3D Euclidean space.

P_ALPHAFOLD_JUMPER.paper_title: Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction with AlphaFold
P_ALPHAFOLD_JUMPER.abstract: Proteins are essential to life. We develop AlphaFold2, an attention-based neural network architecture capable of predicting protein structures to near-experimental atomic accuracy (median backbone RMSD < 1.0 Angstrom) on the CASP14 blind assessment.

sections.heading: Evoformer Architecture and Pair Representations
sections.text: The Evoformer block treats protein modeling as an iterative graph inference problem. It maintains two representations: an MSA representation (N_seq x N_res x d_msa) and a pair representation (N_res x N_res x d_pair). Outer product mean operations transfer evolutionary information from the MSA into spatial distance pair representations.

sections.heading: Invariant Point Attention (IPA) and Structure Module
sections.text: The structure module operates on 3D rigid body frames (T = (R, t) in SE(3)) for each residue. Invariant Point Attention (IPA) combines standard scalar query-key attention with 3D coordinate points in local residue frames, guaranteeing strict SE(3) invariance under global rotations and translations.

P_ESM_RIVES.paper_title: Biological Structure and Function Emerge from Scaling Unsupervised Learning on Sequence Databases
P_ESM_RIVES.abstract: Biological sequence databases contain diverse evolutionary information. We train large language models across 250 million protein sequences (ESM) using masked language modeling, demonstrating that representations learn secondary and tertiary atomic contacts without explicit supervision.

sections.heading: Unsupervised Protein Language Models
sections.text: By training transformer encoders on UniRef sequence corpora, attention heads naturally capture residue-residue contact maps and physicochemical properties, enabling zero-shot mutation fitness prediction and structure estimation directly from single sequences.

SURVEY_SYS_CONSENSUS.paper_title: Consensus Protocols in Distributed Storage and Cloud Computing: A Comparative Survey
SURVEY_SYS_CONSENSUS.abstract: Fault-tolerant distributed systems rely on consensus protocols to maintain state machine replication across unreliable networks. This survey compares crash-fault-tolerant (CFT) protocols including Paxos and Raft against Byzantine-fault-tolerant (BFT) mechanisms, evaluating leader election overhead, log compaction, and formal understandability.

sections.heading: 1. State Machine Replication Fundamentals
sections.text: In replicated state machines, multiple servers execute identical state machine transitions by agreeing on an identical replicated sequence of log commands. The protocol must maintain safety (never return an incorrect result under arbitrary packet delay) and liveness (continue making progress as long as a majority of nodes remain reachable).

sections.heading: 2. Crash Fault Tolerance: Paxos vs Raft
sections.text: While Paxos established the theoretical foundation of distributed consensus, its decomposition into Synod, Multi-Paxos, and lease reads proved notoriously difficult to understand and implement correctly in production. Raft was explicitly designed to improve understandability by decomposing consensus into distinct, independent subproblems: leader election, log replication, and safety invariants.

P_RAFT_ONGARO.paper_title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft)
P_RAFT_ONGARO.abstract: Raft is a consensus algorithm for managing a replicated log. It produces a result equivalent to Multi-Paxos and is as efficient, but its structure is much more understandable, decomposed into leader election, log replication, and membership changes.

sections.heading: 5.1 Raft Basics: Roles and Terms
sections.text: A Raft cluster consists of servers in one of three states: leader, follower, or candidate. Time is divided into arbitrary terms numbered with consecutive integers. Leaders service client requests; followers only respond to RPCs. Raft uses randomized election timers (e.g. 150-300 ms) to resolve split votes during leader election.

sections.heading: 5.4 Safety and Log Matching Property
sections.text: If an entry is committed at a given term and index, Raft guarantees that entry will be present in the logs of the leaders for all higher terms. A voter rejects a candidate whose log is less up-to-date than the voter's own log, enforcing leader completeness.

P_PAXOS_LAMPORT.abstract: The Paxos algorithm, when presented in plain English, is very simple. It guarantees that in an asynchronous network where processors can fail by stopping and messages can be delayed or lost, at most one value can be chosen.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Prepare and Promise
sections.text: A proposer selects a proposal number n and sends a prepare request with number n to a majority of acceptors. If an acceptor receives a prepare request with number n greater than that of any prepare request to which it has already responded, it responds with a promise not to accept any more proposals numbered less than n and with the highest-numbered proposal that it has accepted.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Accept and Accepted
sections.text: If the proposer receives a response to its prepare requests from a majority of acceptors, then it sends an accept request to each of those acceptors for a proposal numbered n with a value v, where v is the value of the highest-numbered proposal among the responses.
